newsitem.title: INDIA: I-Sec sees yield on India 364-day t-bill falling.
newsitem.headline: I-Sec sees yield on India 364-day t-bill falling.

text.p: India's 364-day treasury bill auction yield is expected to fall over the next fortnight, following the one percentage point cut in the central bank's bank rate, ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said.
Both the primary and secondary markets in treasury bills have been extremely dull over the past month, I-Sec said in its latest debt market update released on Wednesday.
Auction yields on treasury bills are constant at previous levels with no difference between cut-off and weighted average yields, indicating a market consensus on the cut-off, it said.
Yields in the secondary market too have been rock steady at previous levels.
"However, with the one percentage point cut in the bank rate, we are likely to see a decline in the 364-day yield over the next fortnight," the I-Sec report said.
It said the 14-day treasury bill introduced in May appeared to be a non-starter in the secondary market.
"Cumulative volume last month was a mere 1.66 billion rupees with no trading since June 17," it said.
"Such a market response casts a doubt whether the maturity selected was the right one and the need for better market feedback before deciding upon the maturity to be introduced."
